facts.statement: The genus Tetronarce was described by T. N. Gill in 1862.
Tetronarce belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, order Torpediniformes, and family Torpedinidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Chondrichthyes superordo: Batoidea ordo: Torpediniformes familia: Torpedinidae

facts.statement: Species in the genus Tetronarce are commonly known as electric rays.
facts.quote: Tetronarce is a genus of ray fish, commonly known as electric rays.

facts.statement: These rays are slow-moving bottom-dwellers that use electricity for both defense and feeding.
facts.quote: They are slow-moving bottom-dwellers capable of generating electricity as a defense and feeding mechanism.

facts.statement: Tetronarce species can grow up to 180 cm in total length, which is significantly larger than the 25 to 80 cm range typical of Torpedo species.
facts.quote: Tetronarce species tend to attain a much larger size of up to 180 cm TL than Torpedo electric rays species, which usually range from 25 to 80 cm TL.

facts.statement: There are nine recognized species within the genus Tetronarce.
facts.quote: There are nine recognized species in this genus

facts.statement: Tetronarce californica is found in the northeastern Pacific Ocean, ranging from Baja California to British Columbia.
facts.quote: Tetronarce californica Ayres, 1855 Pacific electric ray northeastern Pacific Ocean from Baja California to British Columbia.

facts.statement: Tetronarce cowleyi is distributed around southern Africa, from Walvis Bay in Namibia to Algoa Bay in South Africa.
facts.quote: Tetronarce cowleyi Ebert, D. L. Haas & M. R. de Carvalho, 2015 Cowley's torpedo ray around southern Africa, from Walvis Bay, Namibia to Algoa Bay, Eastern Cape, South Africa

facts.statement: Tetronarce fairchildi is endemic to New Zealand.
facts.quote: Tetronarce fairchildi F. W. Hutton, 1872 New Zealand torpedo New Zealand

facts.statement: Tetronarce formosa is found in the Northwest Pacific, specifically in Taiwan.
facts.quote: Tetronarce formosa D. L. Haas & Ebert, 2006 Taiwan torpedo Northwest Pacific: Taiwan.

facts.statement: Tetronarce macneilli inhabits southern Australia, ranging from Port Hedland to the Swain Reefs.
facts.quote: Tetronarce macneilli Whitley, 1932 Shorttail torpedo southern Australia from Port Hedland to the Swain Reefs

facts.statement: Tetronarce nobiliana is found in the Atlantic Ocean, ranging from Nova Scotia to Brazil in the west and from Scotland to West Africa and southern Africa in the east.
facts.quote: Tetronarce nobiliana Bonaparte, 1835 Atlantic torpedo Atlantic Ocean, from Nova Scotia to Brazil in the west and from Scotland to West Africa and off southern Africa in the east

facts.statement: Tetronarce puelcha is found in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.
facts.quote: Tetronarce puelcha Lahille, 1926 Argentine torpedo Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay.

facts.statement: Tetronarce tokionis is found in Japan and Taiwan.
facts.quote: Tetronarce tokionis S. Tanaka (I), 1908 Trapezoid torpedo Japan and Taiwan.

facts.statement: Tetronarce tremens is distributed across Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Peru.
facts.quote: Tetronarce tremens F. de Buen, 1959 Chilean torpedo Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Peru.

facts.statement: Tetronarce ramanamurthyi is found in the Southeastern Arabian Sea.
facts.quote: Tetronarce ramanamurthyi Bineesh, Kasinath, & Ebert, 2026 Ramanamurthy's torpedo ray Southeastern Arabian Sea.

facts.statement: A Spanish source lists 13 species within the genus Tetronarce.
No fossil occurrences for the genus Tetronarce have been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
